## About

I am an Assistant Professor in the Division of Business Administration at Dongduk
Women's University. Three questions organise my work: how AI systems should be governed,
how far they can be trusted as instruments of measurement and simulation, and what the
digital records they produce reveal about risk in financial and housing markets.

Much of what I do begins with a record that was never meant for research — a blockchain
ledger, a municipal permit filing, a mortgage application file — and asks what can be
credibly recovered from it. That commitment runs in both directions: machine learning
lets me read sources that were previously unreadable at scale, and the same scrutiny I
apply to an administrative record I apply to the models themselves, asking where their
answers stop being trustworthy.

Before joining Dongduk, I was a Senior Researcher in the AI Policy Research Division of
the [Software Policy & Research Institute (SPRI)](https://spri.kr), where I led analysis
of AI regulatory trends, impact assessment of high-impact AI systems, and measurement of
the AI industry. I hold a Ph.D. in Management Information Systems from Sogang
University.

## Research interests

::: {.interests}
::: {.interest}
[AI policy and governance]{.k}
[How regulators should assess the impact of high-impact AI systems, and how an AI industry that resists conventional classification can be measured at all.]{.v}
:::

::: {.interest}
[LLM agents for economic and social science]{.k}
[When an LLM-agent testbed can be trusted to answer a mechanism-design question, and how language models can read administrative text into research-grade measures.]{.v}
:::

::: {.interest}
[Graph learning for financial security]{.k}
[Graph neural networks and Transformer architectures that detect fraud and phishing on blockchain transaction networks, under the label scarcity and extreme imbalance that real deployments face.]{.v}
:::

::: {.interest}
[Machine learning in finance and real estate]{.k}
[Deep learning for asset valuation, and machine reading of public records to measure liquidity, displacement, and credit access in housing markets.]{.v}
:::
:::
